title: Car Sickness
desc: Cerenia, acepromazine, dimenhydrinate and meclizine for travel sickness, with separate dog and cat dosing.

meds.name: Cerenia
meds.desc: the licensed drug for motion sickness
meds.note: 8 mg/kg MINIMUM for motion sickness — this is much higher than the anti-emetic dose. Give at least 2 hours before travel.

meds.name: Acepromazine
meds.note: 0.25–2.2 mg/kg for sedation. In a dog on chronic use you may need to double the dosage. Acepromazine sedates but does not stop nausea — pair it with an anti-emetic rather than relying on it alone.

meds.name: Acepromazine
meds.note: Per-cat dose from the source sheet.

meds.name: Dimenhydrinate
meds.note: 5 mg/kg, which works out at about one 50 mg tablet per 20 lb of body weight.

meds.name: Meclizine
meds.note: 0.5 mg/kg. In practice the sheet uses 12.5 mg for a small dog, 25 mg for a big dog, and 50 mg for a very large dog.

notes.Cerenia dose is the catch: Motion sickness needs a MINIMUM of 8 mg/kg — far above the usual anti-emetic dose. Under-dosing is the commonest reason it appears not to work.
notes.Acepromazine with chronic use: In a dog given it repeatedly, the dose may need doubling over time.
notes.Sedation is not anti-nausea: Acepromazine makes a dog quiet but does not stop the nausea. For a dog that actually vomits, pair it with Cerenia or an antihistamine.
notes.Meclizine in practice: 0.5 mg/kg on paper; in practice 12.5 mg for a small dog, 25 mg for a big dog, 50 mg for a very large one.

dischargeBlocks.title: When to give it
dischargeBlocks.text:
Give the medication at least 2 hours before you set off, on a small amount of food.

Giving it as you put {name} in the car is too late — it needs time to be absorbed and working before the journey starts.

dischargeBlocks.title: What else helps
dischargeBlocks.text:
- Withhold food for a few hours before travelling, but leave water available.
- Face {name} forward and, if it is safe, let some fresh air in.
- A crate or a proper travel harness stops sliding around, which makes the sickness worse.
- Keep the car cool.
- Take short, pleasant trips between now and any long journey so the car stops predicting sickness.

dischargeBlocks.title: Try it before the big trip
dischargeBlocks.text:
Please give a trial dose before a short journey rather than saving it for a long trip or a holiday.

That way we know how {name} responds, and can change the dose or the drug if we need to.

dischargeBlocks.title: Follow up
dischargeBlocks.text: Let us know how {name} travelled. If there was still vomiting, or {name} was too sleepy for too long, call us — there are several options and it often takes one adjustment to get it right.
